name: Washington D.C.
tagline: Free Museums, World-Class Culture, and the Heart of American History
description: Washington D.C. is one of the few cities in the world where you can visit dozens of world-class museums entirely for free. The Smithsonian Institution, National Gallery of Art, and countless monuments make it a cultural powerhouse. The Metro system is one of the best in the US, and the city's diverse neighborhoods offer everything from Georgetown's Federal architecture to Adams Morgan's international dining. Housing is expensive and DC has its own income tax, but the unmatched access to free culture and excellent transit partially offset the costs for FIRE retirees.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – varies by neighborhood; many areas are very safe
quickFacts.climate: Humid subtropical with hot summers and cold, occasionally snowy winters

housing.description: Studio in a good Columbia Heights building, or a 1BR in Petworth or Arlington

dining.description: Frugal; mostly cooks, occasional Ethiopian/Salvadoran in Adams Morgan/Mount Pleasant

healthcare.description: A subsidized Silver plan through DC Health Link, assuming annual income stays under the 2026 subsidy cutoff of about $62,600; above that, the plan goes to full price. Priced for ages 45-55; older retirees should budget more.

transportation.description: WMATA Metro monthly pass; DC is very walkable/bikeable

entertainment.description: Free Smithsonians and monuments hold this down

1M.lifestyle: A studio in a good Columbia Heights building or a one-bedroom in Petworth or across the river in Arlington keeps housing within a lean budget, though Washington's floor stays high. The Metro removes the need for a car, health is a MAGI-managed subsidized Silver plan through DC Health Link, and the city's signature perk — dozens of free Smithsonian museums and monuments — keeps entertainment costs near zero. Meals lean on the Ethiopian and Salvadoran spots of Adams Morgan and Mount Pleasant, with most cooking done at home. The District's own income tax tightens an already constrained budget, but few cities give back so much culture for free.

housing.description: Nicer 1BR in Logan Circle, on U Street, or in a newer Columbia Heights building

dining.description: Out a few times a week across the international scene

healthcare.description: Lower-cost Silver or a partially subsidized plan near the cliff, for a ~50yo

entertainment.description: Kennedy Center evenings, museum openings, a gym, Shenandoah hikes

2M.lifestyle: A nicer one-bedroom in Logan Circle, on U Street, or in a newer Columbia Heights building buys a vibrant, walkable neighborhood in the heart of the District. Dining out lands a few times a week across Washington's deep international scene, healthcare is a lower-cost Silver plan or a partially subsidized plan near the cliff, and a Metro pass with regular rideshare covers the compact city. Kennedy Center evenings, museum openings, a gym, and weekend hikes in Shenandoah fill the calendar, with the free Smithsonians always in reserve. A comfortable urban life with culture built in.

housing.description: Quality 1BR or modest 2BR in Georgetown, a Capitol Hill rowhouse, or a Kalorama condo

dining.description: Dining out regularly across the international scene

healthcare.description: Unsubsidized, age-rated DC Health Link plan (Silver/Gold; 45yo ~$690, 55yo ~$1,065), GW/Georgetown/Johns Hopkins access — the swing line above the cliff

transportation.description: Metro plus frequent rideshare and occasional rental

3M.lifestyle: A quality one-bedroom or modest two-bedroom in Georgetown, a Capitol Hill rowhouse, or a Kalorama condo puts daily life in Washington's most walkable, established neighborhoods. Dining out is a regular habit across the city's international scene, and healthcare is a full-price, age-rated plan with GW, Georgetown, and nearby Johns Hopkins access — the swing line above the returned ACA cliff. Metro, rideshare, and an occasional rental cover errands and weekend drives to Virginia wine country or the Chesapeake. Kennedy Center performances, Nationals games, and the free museums make for a rich calendar. At $6,800 a month, Washington is comfortably affluent, with an intellectual, policy-tinged social scene.

housing.description: Large luxury condo in Georgetown or Kalorama

healthcare.description: Top plan plus concierge / direct-primary-care (GW, Sibley), Johns Hopkins access

transportation.description: Private car service with garage parking

entertainment.description: Kennedy Center / National Gallery patronage, Nationals box seats

luxuryExtras.description: Club memberships, concierge, Virginia horse-country weekends, travel fund

5M.lifestyle: A large luxury condo in Georgetown or Kalorama, with a housekeeper on a weekly rhythm, marks an upper-affluent Washington life. Fine dining is a near-daily option, healthcare adds a concierge or direct-primary-care retainer to a top plan with Johns Hopkins access, and a private car service with garage parking handles the city and weekends in Virginia horse country. Patron-level involvement at the Kennedy Center and the National Gallery, Nationals box seats, and business-class travel are all comfortable. Washington's social world skews intellectual and policy-oriented, which suits a certain retirement well.

housing.description: Historic Kalorama mansion, Georgetown estate, or Embassy Row property — full estates rent $10k–18k+; this prices a grand residence below that ceiling

dining.description: Frequent fine dining with occasional private-chef evenings

healthcare.description: Top plan plus full concierge (GW/Sibley) and Johns Hopkins specialist access

transportation.description: Private car / luxury vehicle with garage

entertainment.description: Smithsonian/Kennedy Center board-level patronage, galas, art

luxuryExtras.description: Clubs, art, first-class travel, a Virginia weekend property

10M.lifestyle: A historic Kalorama mansion, a Georgetown estate, or an Embassy Row property, kept by a housekeeper with part-time help, anchors life at the top of Washington. Dining is frequent at the finest tables, with the occasional private-chef evening in, healthcare is a top plan with full concierge care at GW or Sibley and Johns Hopkins specialist access, and a private car handles the city and the Virginia countryside. Smithsonian and Kennedy Center patronage at the board level, galas, art collecting, and a weekend property in horse country are all comfortable, along with first-class travel. This is established, cultured wealth in a city whose intellectual and diplomatic life runs deep.
